#SciFeature 𝗥𝗔𝗠𝗦𝗔𝗥 𝗦𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗦 𝗜𝗡 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗣𝗛𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗣𝗣𝗜𝗡𝗘𝗦 

Wetlands are among the planet’s most valuable ecosystems. From mangrove forests and rivers to coral-rich lagoons and marshes, these water-filled landscapes provide food and freshwater, reduce flooding, store carbon, regulate climate, and serve as vital habitats for countless species of plants and animals.

Recognizing their importance, nations gathered in Ramsar, Iran, and on February 2, 1971, signed a landmark environmental treaty for wetland conservation. Today, more than 2,500 Ramsar Sites around the world are recognized as Wetlands of International Importance.

In the Philippines, wetlands come in many forms: seagrass beds, mangroves, estuaries, mudflats, swamps, lakes, caves, and even human-made areas such as rice fields, dams, and fishponds. 

According to the Atlas of Philippine Wetlands and Classified Caves, the country is home to 342 wetlands covering more than 380,000 hectares. Among these, eight wetlands have earned international recognition as Ramsar Sites:

[𝟭] 𝗢𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗼 𝗜𝘀𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗪𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗹𝗶𝗳𝗲 𝗦𝗮𝗻𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗿𝘆
Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu 

[𝟮] 𝗧𝘂𝗯𝗯𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗵𝗮 𝗥𝗲𝗲𝗳𝘀 𝗡𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗸
Cagayancillo, Palawan

[𝟯] 𝗔𝗴𝘂𝘀𝗮𝗻 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝘀𝗵 𝗪𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗹𝗶𝗳𝗲 𝗦𝗮𝗻𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗿𝘆
Agusan del Sur

[𝟰] 𝗡𝗮𝘂𝗷𝗮𝗻 𝗟𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗡𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗸
Oriental Mindoro 

[𝟱] 𝗣𝘂𝗲𝗿𝘁𝗼 𝗣𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗲𝘀𝗮 𝗦𝘂𝗯𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗿𝗮𝗻𝗲𝗮𝗻 𝗥𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗡𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗸
Puerto Princesa, Palawan 

[𝟲] 𝗟𝗮𝘀 𝗣𝗶𝗻𝗮𝘀-𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗾𝘂𝗲 𝗖𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗛𝗮𝗯𝗶𝘁𝗮𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗘𝗰𝗼𝘁𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗺 𝗔𝗿𝗲𝗮 (𝗟𝗣𝗣𝗖𝗛𝗘𝗔)
Metro Manila

[𝟳] 𝗡𝗲𝗴𝗿𝗼𝘀 𝗢𝗰𝗰𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗖𝗼𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗪𝗲𝘁𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱𝘀 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗔𝗿𝗲𝗮 (𝗡𝗢𝗖𝗪𝗖𝗔)
Negros Occidental

[𝟴] 𝗦𝗮𝘀𝗺𝘂𝗮𝗻 𝗣𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗮 𝗖𝗼𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗪𝗲𝘁𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱𝘀
Pampanga

We can help protect wetlands by reducing pollution, conserving water, planting mangroves and native vegetation responsibly, practicing proper waste disposal, supporting conservation efforts, and preventing illegal dumping, overfishing, and destructive land conversion activities. #Wetlands #OceanMonth

data.text:
🌳🪾“57,000 seedlings.” 🪾🌳- Madami at magandang pakinggan. Magandang headline din. Pero hindi nito agad mapapalitan ang ecological function ng 600 mature trees na pinutol sa Metro Manila. 🪵🪵🪵🪵🪵

Sa panahon ng matinding urban heat, climate anxiety, at lumalalang pagbaha, ang mature trees ay hindi dekorasyon o obstruction sa infrastructure. Silent public servants sila ng lungsod. Libre silang nagpapalamig. Sumisipsip ng tubig-ulan. Nagfi-filter ng polusyon. Nagbabawas ng stress. Nagbibigay ng dignidad sa paglalakad sa siyudad.

Ang problema sa maraming development framework ngayon: masyadong nakatingin sa quantity kaysa ecological integrity. Seedlings are future possibilities. Mature trees are present protection. Hindi linear ang kapalit. Hindi puwedeng spreadsheet mentality lang ang environmental governance.

Ilang dekada bago maabot ng seedlings ang parehong canopy cover, carbon storage, cooling effect, at biodiversity support ng mature trees? Ilan ang mabubuhay? Ilan ang matatamaan ulit ng susunod na road widening? Ilan ang tunay na maitatanim sa highly urbanized spaces?

Ito ang delikadong kultura ng “offset mentality” — puwedeng sirain ngayon basta may ipapangakong kapalit bukas. Pero sa climate crisis, delayed ecological recovery is also social injustice. Ang pinaka-apektado sa pagkawala ng urban trees ay hindi ang naka-aircon. Kundi ang commuter, street vendor, traffic enforcer, delivery rider, estudyante, at ordinaryong mamamayang direktang niluluto ng urban heat.

At malinaw na panahon na upang paghiwalayin ang regulatory at environmental protection functions sa loob ng DENR. Hindi puwedeng iisang sistema ang parehong nagpo-promote, nag-aapprove, at dapat nagpo-protekta sa kalikasan. Kapag magkalaban ang mandato, kadalasan talo ang ecological integrity.

Ang tunay na sustainable city hindi lang measured sa dami ng kalsada at bilis ng sasakyan. Sinusukat din ito sa dami ng punong nananatili, kalidad ng hangin, walkability, biodiversity, at kapasidad ng lungsod na protektahan ang buhay sa gitna ng climate extremes.

Kapag mature trees ang unang sinasakripisyo para sa “development,” kailangang tanungin: development para kanino? 🌿🏙️🔥

#ProtectUrbanTrees #ClimateJustice #LaudatoSi #ManilaNeedsTrees
